predecessors.name: Phoenicia
predecessors.text: the site of Carthage, 'settled around 814 BC by merchants from Tyre'

predecessors.name: Phoenician colonies
predecessors.text: the western colonies (Sardinia, Sicily, Malta, southern Iberia) without Cyprus

successors.name: Roman Republic
successors.text: 'the annexation of all remaining Carthaginian territory by Rome'; the territories were 'reconstituted to become the Roman province of Africa, with Utica as its capital'

ledger.x: 814 BC: Tyrian merchants settle Carthage.
7th century BC: the western Phoenician colonies pass to Carthage.
6th-5th century BC: the Magonids build the African and western Mediterranean domain.
480 BC: Hanno II's reign begins (480-440) and the African coast fills out.
5th century BC: the Libyan and Moroccan interior and all of Sardinia.
409 BC: Hannibal Mago takes Selinus and destroys Himera.
406 BC: Carthage storms Akragas and Gela.
405 BC: Dionysius I makes peace.
405 BC: the Greek cities of southern Sicily pay tribute to Carthage.
398 BC: Dionysius I breaks the peace and strikes Motya.
396 BC: the vassal cities are lost.
393 BC: peace with Syracuse.
Corsica passes to Carthage; 384 BC is a bridge, not a page date.
311 BC: Agathocles invades the last Carthaginian holdings.
311 BC: Hamilcar wins the rest of Sicily.
306 BC: Agathocles negotiates peace.
306 BC: Carthage keeps only the west of Sicily.
277 BC: Pyrrhus takes Eryx.
275 BC: Carthage recovers western Sicily.
265 BC: a Carthaginian fleet takes the harbour of Messina.
264 BC: Rome lands in Sicily at Messana.
264 BC: the Mamertines expel the Carthaginian garrison.
261 BC: Rome takes Akragas.
256 BC: Regulus lands in Africa and takes Tunis.
255 BC: Xanthippus beats Regulus.
254 BC: Rome takes Panormus.
252 BC: Rome burns Selinous and Heraclea Minoa.
241 BC: the Treaty of Lutatius.
241 BC: the First Punic War ends with the Battle of the Aegates Islands and the Treaty of Lutatius.
Late 241 BC: the mercenaries make Tunis their base.
239 BC: Utica and Hippo go over to the rebels.
238 BC: the Libyan revolt is crushed.
237 BC: Rome takes Sardinia and Corsica.
237 BC: Hamilcar Barca lands at Gades.
229 BC: Hamilcar's four years of campaigns reach Cape Nao.
220 BC: Hannibal completes the conquest of Hispania south of the Ebro.
219 BC: Hannibal takes Saguntum.
218 BC: Rome lodges itself in north-east Iberia.
218 BC: Cliopatria's shape reaches north of the Ebro, with no page behind it.
Nov 218 BC: Hannibal reaches Cisalpine Gaul.
215 BC: Hasdrubal is beaten at Dertosa.
213 BC: Carthage holds Agrigentum again.
210 BC: Agrigentum is betrayed to Rome.
209 BC: Scipio storms Carthago Nova.
209 BC: Carthago Nova falls.
208 BC: Scipio wins at Baecula.
206 BC: Ilipa and Gades end Carthaginian Iberia.
206 BC: the Iberian war ends at Ilipa and Gades.
204 BC: Scipio lands in Africa.
203 BC: Hannibal leaves Italy.
Oct 202 BC: Zama.
201 BC: Carthage is stripped of its overseas territories.
201 BC: Carthage becomes a Roman client.
Early 2nd century BC: Masinissa strips the Libyan and Algerian coast.
Early 2nd century BC: the Moroccan strips pass to Mauretania.
149 BC: Utica goes over to Rome.
149 BC: Rome lands at Utica and besieges Carthage.
Spring 146 BC: the assault on Carthage ends the siege.
146 BC: the client state ends with the city.
Spring 146 BC: Scipio Aemilianus destroys Carthage.

wars.name: Carthaginian expeditions against Sardinia
wars.outcome: Carthage subdues the coasts and the south; by the 509 treaty with Rome it is treated as Carthaginian.

wars.name: Carthaginian invasion of Sicily and the Battle of Himera
wars.outcome: Hamilcar was 'decisively defeated by Gelo at the Battle of Himera'; Carthage paid reparations ('2,000 talents'), stayed out of Sicily for about 70 years and lost no territory.

wars.name: Sicilian War of 409-405 BC
wars.outcome: Hannibal Mago took Selinus and Himera (409); in 406-405 Carthage sacked Akragas, took Gela, sacked Camarina and beat Dionysius I.

wars.name: Sicilian War of 398-392 BC
wars.outcome: Dionysius broke the peace and struck Motya; Himilco retook it and captured Messina; in 396 Carthage 'lost her new Greek conquests but retained control over the western territories'.

wars.name: Sicilian War of 383-376 BC
wars.outcome: Dionysius reopened hostilities in 383; he beat the Carthaginians at Cabala (378) and Mago III won at Cronium (376); the peace made Dionysius pay 1,000 talents and left Carthage 'in control of Western Sicily'.

wars.name: Sicilian War of 345-339 BC (Timoleon)
wars.outcome: Timoleon's expedition ended with the Carthaginians defeated at the Crimissus in 339; the treaty left Carthage 'territories west of the Halycas river'.

wars.name: Agathocles' war with Carthage
wars.outcome: Agathocles seized Messana (315), invaded the last Carthaginian holdings (311), was beaten at the Himera River, landed in Africa, and negotiated a treaty in 306 that left him the eastern half of Sicily.

wars.name: Pyrrhus in Sicily
wars.outcome: Pyrrhus lifted the siege of Syracuse (278), took Eryx (277), demanded Carthage 'abandon all of Sicily', failed at Lilybaeum after two months (276) and left; Carthage kept Lilybaeum.

wars.name: First Punic War
wars.outcome: Rome took Akragas (261), Panormus (254) and the hold-outs of the west (252); Carthage held only Lilybaeum and Drepana by 248, Eryx from 247; after the Aegates Islands (241) 'Carthage evacuated Sicily' and paid 3,200 talents.

wars.name: Mercenary War
wars.outcome: About 20,000 unpaid soldiers mutinied, the Libyan towns rose, Utica and Hippo killed their garrisons (239); Hamilcar Barca won at the Bagradas, the Saw and Leptis Parva (238) and the revolt was over 'by the winter of 238 BC'.

wars.name: Barcid conquest of Iberia
wars.outcome: Hamilcar landed at Gades (237), subdued the Turdetani and the area to Cape Nao and founded Akra Leuke (c.

wars.name: Second Punic War
wars.outcome: Rome expelled Carthage from Iberia (Carthago Nova 209, Baecula 208, Ilipa and Gades 206), Hannibal left Italy, and Scipio won at Zama (October 202).

wars.name: Carthaginian-Numidian war of 151 BC
wars.outcome: Carthage counter-attacked Masinissa despite the 201 treaty; its army was beaten at Oroscopa and surrendered; Rome used the breach as its pretext.

wars.name: Third Punic War
wars.outcome: Utica went over to Rome (149), the Romans landed and besieged Carthage; Scipio Aemilianus took sole command (147) and assaulted the city in spring 146; Carthage was destroyed and its territory became the Roman province of Africa.

certainty.note: Ancient frontiers throughout: the African interior, the Libyan coast and the Numidian frontier were never surveyed.
